title: Overload isolation policy: adaptive thresholds for 429s, timeouts, and error spikes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement an overload isolation policy that automatically detects and protects routes, tenants, and regions from cascading failures by (a) triggering progressive isolation actions on 429 spikes, timeouts, and elevated error rates and (b) exposing clear telemetry and safe rollback behavior.

Design summary:
- Three layered trigger windows:
  1) Instant burst window (1m): measure 429 spike rate and tail timeouts. Soft-mitigation trigger when 429_rate > 1% OR timeout_count >= 5 in 1m.
  2) Sustained degradation window (5m): sustained tail latency or increasing error_rate. Hard-mitigation when 95p_latency > 2s for 5m OR error_rate > 3% in 5m.
  3) Critical failure window (15m): circuit open if upstream error_rate > 5% OR consecutive timeouts > 10 in 15m.

- Mitigation actions (progressive):
  - Soft degrade: apply short (30s) rate-limited throttling to non-priority customers, increase KV cache TTL for repeated prefixes, enable local batching.
  - Model variant downgrade: route to smaller, compatible model variant (e.g., from mixture-1 to mixture-1-compact) with deterministic quality guardrails.
  - Route quarantine: move traffic to a standby pool/dedicated capacity if available.
  - Circuit open: stop forwarding to problematic variant/region for a configurable cool-down and surface stubbed responses or 503s with structured retry hints.
  - Half-open probing: allow sampled probes (1-5% of traffic) after cooldown to validate recovery before fully closing the circuit.

Key constraints and trade-offs:
- Latency vs. quality: variant downgrade reduces cost/latency but may change outputs. We require per-route quality checks (A/B prompt set) and automatic rollback if semantic regressions exceed tolerance.
- Per-tenant correctness: default policy is conservative for customers flagged as high-SLA; they must opt-in to automatic model downgrades.
- Observability surface: every trigger must emit structured events with reason codes (e.g., TR_429_SPIKE, TR_TIMEOUTS, TR_ERR_RATE) and include pre/post metrics slices for debugging.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Implement trigger engine library in runtime that consumes streaming metrics (429s, timeouts, latency histograms, error rates). Expose policy DSL for per-route, per-tenant overrides.
2) Implement mitigation actuators: downgrade-route, apply-throttle, quarantine-route, open-circuit, probe-route.
3) Feature flag + canary: ship behind feature flag; canary rollout to 5% of routes, then 25% with telemetry gating.
4) Dashboards & alerts: create a per-route SLO dashboard, add three derived metrics and a composite "isolation_state" time-series.
5) QA: run fault-injection tests in staging with synthetic 429s and injected timeouts; measure false-positive rate and median time-to-recover for half-open probing.

Acceptable default numeric thresholds (tunable):
- 1m window: 429_rate > 1% => soft-mitigation
- 5m window: error_rate > 3% or 95p_latency > 2s => hard-mitigation
- 15m window: error_rate > 5% or consecutive_timeouts >= 10 => open circuit
- Cooldown default: 5 minutes; probe sampling: 2%

Rollout & safety:
- Default policies are conservative and can be overridden by per-customer policies.
- Every mitigation must emit a human-readable rollback reason and allow manual override from Console.
- Start with read-only telemetry in stage for two weeks before enabling actuators.

Open decisions:
- Exact default numeric thresholds (current numbers are proposals; need perf benchmarks).
- How to store per-tenant opt-in for model downgrades (Console toggle vs. API flag).
- Interaction with Dedicated capacity autoscaling (quota vs. quarantine behavior).
